name: Sebamed

lead: Sebamed is a German skincare brand built around cleansers formulated at pH 5.5, close to the skin's naturally slightly acidic surface. Its pitch is gentle, soap-free cleansing that leaves the skin barrier intact, which supporters link to less dryness, irritation and flaking.

The brand was founded in 1967 by dermatologist Heinz Maurer and is sold in more than 100 countries. Small studies have used its products as comparators or test moisturizers in infant and adult skin research.

paras: People use it as a bar or liquid wash for face and body, as a baby cleanser, and as a lotion or cream. It is often part of a minimal routine for sensitive or dry skin.
As a cosmetic wash and lotion it is generally well tolerated in the trials listed; as with any product, individual irritation or allergy is possible.

angle.text: Sebamed positions its cleansers as removing dirt without stripping the skin's surface, so skin stays comfortable and less flaky. People use it as a gentle base in a skincare routine.

lead: Sebamed is a German dermatological skincare brand, made by Sebapharma, known for soap-free cleansers formulated at pH 5.5 to match the skin's acid mantle.[1] People use it to cleanse without the dryness and tightness associated with alkaline soaps, keeping skin comfortable and its surface looking calmer.

According to the brand's history, dermatologist Heinz Maurer observed in the early 1950s that alkaline soaps aggravated eczema patients and developed a pH 5.5 synthetic-detergent alternative; the first commercial bar launched in 1967 under Sebamat GmbH in Boppard, Germany.[1] A liquid face and body wash followed in 1970 and a lotion in 1974.[1]

Published research includes a randomized trial in 180 infants comparing Sebamed Baby Liquid, another baby cleanser and plain water, which found all three well tolerated,[2] and a study in which two weeks of Sebamed lotion thickened the epidermis and reduced skin-fold width in participants of three ethnic groups.[3]
infobox: Sebapharma GmbH & Co. KG, Boppard, Germany

paras: Maurer, working at the University Dermatology Clinic in Bonn, is described as recognizing in 1952 that soaps with a pH of roughly 9 to 10 aggravated eczema, and as trialing a pH 5.5 cleanser; he founded Sebamat in 1967.[1] Sebapharma was set up in 1983 as the sales company and moved to Bad Salzig in 1984, and the brand says it sells in over 100 countries.[1]

The range includes cleansing bars, liquid washes, shampoos, lotions and creams for babies, adults and sensitive skin.[1] The central claim is that cleansers matching the skin's slightly acidic pH protect the acid mantle and barrier.[1]

In a randomized controlled trial of 180 healthy infants, Sebamed Baby Liquid, a Johnson's cleanser and lukewarm tap water used twice weekly for two weeks all produced no significant erythema, edema, dryness or scaling and were well tolerated.[2] In 30 women of European, Asian and Black ethnicity, two weeks of Sebamed lotion on one forearm produced a thicker epidermis on optical coherence tomography and narrower skin folds on confocal microscopy than the untreated arm.[3] A laboratory study found Sebamed's intimate wash inhibited some vaginal pathogens in a broth test, with a formulation of Andrographis paniculata inhibiting more.[4]
